Outcome test

Source: R/disp.R
outtst.Rd

The stop rate and the hit rate of a group searched whenever the chance of guilt exceeds a threshold. Hit rates compare averages, not thresholds: two groups held to the same threshold can show different hit rates, and a group held to a lower threshold can show the higher one (infra-marginality). See proof("outtst").

Usage

outtst(q, t, w = NULL)

Arguments

q

The chances of guilt in the group: numbers in the interval 0 to 1.

t

The search threshold: one number.

w

NULL for equal weights, or one non-negative weight per element of q with a positive total; when both are named with unique names, w is matched to q by name.

Value

A named numeric vector: stop (the weighted share searched) and hit (the weighted mean chance of guilt among them; NaN when nobody is searched).

References

Ayres, I. (2002). Outcome tests of racial disparities in police practices. Justice Research and Policy, 4(1-2), 131-142. doi:10.3818/JRP.4.1.2002.131

Simoiu, C., Corbett-Davies, S. and Goel, S. (2017). The problem of infra-marginality in outcome tests for discrimination. The Annals of Applied Statistics, 11(3), 1193-1216. doi:10.1214/17-AOAS1058

Examples

outtst(q = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9), t = 0.3)
#>      stop       hit 
#> 0.6666667 0.7000000
